signal: Compyl raised a $12M Series A led by Venture Guides, doubled its customer base two years running, and is expanding into healthcare, fintech, and APAC with an AI Compliance Copilot.

email.body1:
John, saw Compyl closed its $12M Series A and is expanding into healthcare, fintech, and APAC.

Doubling customers two years running usually means more in-market accounts in play than the team can cover, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Compyl off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
John, quick follow-up for Compyl.

Post-raise and pushing into new verticals, board expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't know how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Compyl needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
John, last bit of proof for Compyl.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Compyl's reply rate likely compares to other Series-A startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
John, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The fundraise-plus-expansion stretch is its own kind of busy, and timing is everything.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a Series-A motion? I'll tailor it to Compyl either way.
